certificate.failed_edge: The inference from the asserted equality involving an undefined function f to the conclusion that (f_n) has no uniform limit is incomplete.
certificate.quote: The sequence $\left(f_n\right)_n$ does not converge uniformly, since given $0<\varepsilon<1$ and $N \in \mathbb{Z}_{+}$, for $x=\varepsilon^{1 / N}$ we have $d\left(f_N(x), f(x)\right)=\varepsilon$.
certificate.reason: The function $f$ has not been defined or shown to be the pointwise limit. One must establish that $f_n(x)\to f(x)$ where $f(x)=0$ for $0\le x<1$ and $f(1)=1$, and that any uniform limit must equal this pointwise limit. Then, fixing for example $\varepsilon=1/2$, for every $N$ the choice $x=(1/2)^{1/N}<1$ gives $|f_N(x)-f(x)|=1/2$, contradicting uniform convergence.

problem.theorem: Define $f_{n}:[0,1] \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ by the equation $f_{n}(x)=x^{n}$. Show that the sequence $\left(f_{n}\right)$ does not converge uniformly.

target_node.claim: Asserts nonuniform convergence using the witness $x=\varepsilon^{1/N}$ and the equality $d(f_N(x),f(x))=\varepsilon$.
target_node.text:
\begin{proof}

    The sequence $\left(f_n\right)_n$ does not converge uniformly, since given $0<\varepsilon<1$ and $N \in \mathbb{Z}_{+}$, for $x=\varepsilon^{1 / N}$ we have $d\left(f_N(x), f(x)\right)=\varepsilon$.
